page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The compute configuration is backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX and AVX-512F alongside cryptographic AES acceleration.

The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring attached network-based block storage volumes for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded throughput contrasted with lower single-core capabilities. The CPU delivers 11,773.91 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a multi-core Geekbench score of 5,885.0, both placing in the middle 50% category. In contrast, single-threaded metrics register in the bottom quartile, including a single-core stress-ng score of 1,109.07, a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0, and poor single-threaded compression throughput. Memory read performance reaches 71.56 GB/s for large uncached blocks and 656.4 GB/s for small cached blocks, while write throughput sits at 49.43 GB/s.

In operational benchmark profiles, the instance achieved 11.76 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 7.93 GB/s in static web serving throughput, and middle-tier scores in Clang software compilation and PassMark database operations. Small 135M model LLM prompt processing reaches 819.97 tokens per second, but medium 7B model generation falls to 8.51 tokens per second.

Given its resource balance, the ecs.g5.4xlarge offers moderate resource density for enterprise software deployments that rely on multi-threaded execution rather than peak single-thread frequency. The lack of bundled local disks and specialized hardware accelerators makes it best suited for general application hosting, backend API services, mid-tier web serving, build compilation pipelines, and caching nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running on the KVM hypervisor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory for a standard 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. The server features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, operates without bundled local storage, and includes no GPU hardware. Benchmark results reveal mid-tier multi-threaded execution, producing 11.76 million Redis SET operations per second and solid software compilation throughput, contrasted by weak single-threaded performance in compression and instruction tests. The absence of local NVMe storage requires attached block devices for persistent I/O. As a balanced compute platform, the ecs.g5.4xlarge is suited for standard web application serving, CI/CD compilation, enterprise backend microservices, and distributed caching systems.
